findings.title: website_name bypasses the TL0/anonymous restriction that hides website, exposing the same URL's host and path to anonymous visitors
findings.description:
`website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (`user_serializer.rb:105-111`). That macro omits it whenever `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true (`user_serializer.rb:25-33`), which is TL0 and anonymous (`lib/guardian/user_guardian.rb:58-60`). The diff adds `:website_name` to the `attributes` list (line 43) but not to `untrusted_attributes`. Its only guard is `include_website_name` (lines 153-155), which checks `website.present?` and never checks restriction.

Path from input to leak: an anonymous visitor views a TL0 user whose `website` is `http://example.com/user`. `website` is omitted, but `website_name` still returns `example.com/user` (same domain) or `example.com` (other domain) computed from the same `object.user_profile.website`. On the HTML path the JSON is preloaded (`app/controllers/users_controller.rb:51`) and rendered by `user.hbs:66-71`. The `@restrict_fields` flag hides bio and the meta description (`app/views/users/show.html.erb:3-11`), but not this name.

The existing spec's untrusted-attribute list (`spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:11-14`) omits `website_name`, so the leak goes undetected.

Fix: add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` and delete the `include_website_name` method at lines 153-155. The macro then generates `include_website_name?` with the restriction check, and `send(attr).present?` covers the blank-website case. Deleting the method is required, because the `def` in the class body would otherwise override the generated one.

findings.title: include_website_name lacks the `?` suffix, so its website.present? guard never runs and website_name: null is serialized for users with no website
findings.description:
Every other inclusion guard in this file uses the `include_<attr>?` form (for example lines 117, 161, 169, 223). AMS 0.8.3 consults `include_<attr>?`, the same hook that `untrusted_attributes` depends on (lines 25-33, spec lines 13-15). `include_website_name` (no `?`) is therefore never consulted, and `website.present?` at line 154 never runs. For a user with no website, the JSON contains `"website_name": null` (line 43) instead of omitting the key. The guard is dead code, and the spec does not test a blank website, so this goes unnoticed.

The same fix as the finding above (use `untrusted_attributes` and delete this method) resolves this too.

findings.title: Host comparison at line 141 is case-sensitive, so an uppercase-host website drops its path on the same-domain forum
findings.description: `URI#host` preserves case. For `website = "http://Example.com/user"` on a forum whose hostname is `example.com`, line 141 compares `"Example.com" == "example.com"` and fails. The branch at line 144 requires more than two labels, so it is skipped. Line 149 then checks `"example.com".ends_with?(".Example.com")`, which is false. The result is `Example.com` with no path, where the same-domain branch at lines 142-143 intends to show the path. This is cosmetic. The fix is to downcase `website_host` before comparing.
